thread:
pagerduty-bot: 🚨 Paging: #INC-5182 - Ingress 5xx spike in euc2-a (detected by latency alerts)

alex.m: I'm on it. Got the PD page. seeing 502/504 surge in our ingest metrics for euc2-a.

simone: thanks alex. can you confirm if it's ALB/NLB or envoys? dashboards look like fronting proxy 502s.

alex.m: digging into logs now. quick curl against a few backends returns 200 but the ALB health checks are failing intermittently. suggest a probe race.

lia: i see connreset patterns in envoy logs: `stream reset, code: 2` when healthchecks hit backend. timestamps line up with spike start ~1748001000.

ops-rotation: tagging oncall to confirm scope: support tickets show ~6% of requests failing, started ~14:20 UTC and still ongoing.

support-engineer: customers in EU report upload failures and webhooks retry storms. ticket flood increasing. can we give ETA?

alex.m: initial hypothesis: ALB healthcheck timeout + pod readiness race + envoy keepalive/idle timeout mismatch -> connection resets. might be amplified by autoscaler killing warm pods.

ingress-bot: Incident created: #INC-5182 | Severity: P1 | Runbook: ingress-5xx-spike. Please run handoff when stabilised.

simone: immediate mitigations: 1) increase ALB healthcheck timeout from 5s -> 10s 2) bump envoy keepalive to 90s 3) scale ingress controller to +2 replicas in euc2-a 4) weighted DNS shift to euc2-b at 70% if needed.

alex.m: executing step 1 now. patching ALB target group healthcheck interval/timeout.

alex.m: patched. healthcheck timeout -> 10s, interval 15s. give it 2 cycles.

lia: while we wait, i'll increase ingress replicas: `kubectl -n ingress scale deploy/ingress-controller --replicas=5` on euc2-a.

support-engineer: running a quick canary against euc2-a after scale: `curl -H 'Host: api.redwood' https://euc2-a.ingress:443/health` -> 200. but upstream still shows some resets.

alex.m: logs show fewer healthcheck fails but still intermittent. adding Envoy retry policy for 502/504 to reduce customer impact.

simone: good. also let's prepare DNS shift plan if it doesn't stabilise in 10m. ops-rotation, can you coordinate with infra to prepare Route53 weighted change and TTL drop?

ops-rotation: on it. lowering ingress region TTL to 30s and preparing weighted failover to euc2-b at 60%. infra will standby for cut.

lia: applied envoy retry config: 3 retries for 502/503 on local-envoy route. monitoring for duplicate side-effects.

alex.m: after the retry policy and scale we see error rate drop from 6% -> 1.5% over last 3 minutes. latency okay.

support-engineer: informing affected customers: initial message posted to status with note 'degraded API responses for EU customers; mitigation in progress'.

ingress-bot: Alert: ALB healthcheck flaps decreased but not resolved. 15 minute window still showing occasional failures.

simone: we should still plan DNS shift as precaution. let's go 60/40 to euc2-b now to reduce blast radius but keep some traffic for validation.

ops-rotation: executing weighted shift: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://shift-60-40.json` - submitted. TTL already reduced.

alex.m: shift applied. watch metrics in 60s.

lia: verifying ingress in euc2-b is healthy. no 5xxs there.

support-engineer: after shift, customer error volume dropped another notch. tickets queue stabilising.

alex.m: quick postmortem notes: root cause likely a probe/timeout configuration mismatch combined with an aggressive pod churn window during a rolling update earlier (autorepair scale). ALB healthchecks were timing out and Envoy interpreted as upstream resets.

simone: follow-ups: 1) align ALB healthcheck and pod readiness probe timings 2) add a pre-drain grace window during rolling restarts 3) add automated brittle-probe detector to alert before client impact 4) run a canary of rolling updates against euc2-a with lower concurrency.

ops-rotation: assigning follow-ups to infra and eng-runtime. will schedule a post-incident review.

support-engineer: update status page: 'mitigated, partial impact, reduced errors. full recovery in progress.' reaching out to top affected customers with apology + RCA timeline.

alex.m: handing off to simone for formal postmortem. I'll stay nearby for any remaining flapping.

simone: thanks. i'll open the incident doc and start RCA. tagging this as mitigated at 1748005200. great teamwork. :raised_hands:
